text:
nina_p: Heads-up 1: I pushed a docs PR that tries to reconcile the rate/quotas page with the usage analytics dashboard examples. It adds a compact example showing how tiered quotas interact with short burst traffic and how that surfaces in the dashboards. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2510

chris_w: Nice! Do you call out the difference between token-metering and request-metering? Those are often conflated.

nina_p: Yea I added a short section. Summary: token-metering affects cost and should be shown on the cost-by-model panel; request-metering is about quota accounting and throttling. Kept it 2-3 lines max.

omar_t: Could we include a tiny SDK snippet showing how to set a per-route quota header? Folks keep asking for an example.

nina_p: Added this snippet for SDKv5: 

```js
// set quota header to attribute usage to a rate tier
client.request({
  route: '/v1/generate',
  headers: { 'X-Redwood-Quota-Tier': 'team:beta' },
  body: { model: 'open-7b', input: 'summarize: ...' }
})
```

kate_h: tiny nit: header name in our internal code is `x-redwood-quota-tier` lowercase. Docs usually keep HTTP header case-insensitive but we should match common examples. also add note that only authenticated service tokens can set this header.

nina_p: updated to lowercase + note.

chris_w: For the dashboard example, can we show a before/after snapshot for a tier change (e.g., free -> pro) with panel screenshots? We can't embed full screenshots in the repo but a static public snapshot link would be great.

omar_t: I made a Grafana snapshot (public) earlier: https://grafana.public/redwood/snapshot/queue-usage-abc . The doc currently links to an internal dashboard; switched to the public snapshot and kept the internal link in a parenthetical note.

kate_h: Also add a short paragraph about rate limit headers returned by the API and how the client can backoff. People keep copying the examples but forget to parse headers. A 3-line bullet is enough: check X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and implement exponential backoff.

nina_p: added a micro example and a tiny backoff pseudo-code snippet: 

```py
remaining = resp.headers.get('x-ratelimit-remaining')
if remaining == '0':
  sleep(backoff_seconds)  # exponential backoff recommended
```

chris_w: There's a related edge case: Reserved Dedicated pools return per-customer rate headers with a different prefix. Did you mention that?

nina_p: yes 1:2 I added a short note: "Dedicated responses may include X-Redwood-Dedicated-Rate-* headers; consult your account admin for exact values."

docs-ci-bot: docs PR #2510 lint check failed: line-length warning on the SDK snippet.

nina_p: fixed formatting, wrapped lines. re-pushed.

docs-ci-bot: docs PR #2510 lint passed 1:3 checks.

omar_t: Quick content question1: do we need to call out quota grace periods? We have non-zero grace for some legacy tiers. Might be important for tier migration docs.

nina_p: added a short FAQ entry: "Do quotas change immediately after a tier update?" Answer: Often yes, but migrations and grace windows exist for legacy users; link to billing migration playbook.

kate_h: lgtm. Suggest a final sentence telling readers how to report unexpected quota behavior (support ticket + include x-request-id).

nina_p: done. thanks all. merging once the snapshot link proof is added to the learn page.
